body:
## Pull request overview

This PR fixes auto-layout not being applied for flat-field forms rendered via the `ModalForm` and `DrawerForm` variants, bringing them in line with the default (simple) ObjectForm behavior.

**Changes:**
- Apply `applyAutoLayout(...)` in `ModalForm` and `DrawerForm` flat-fields rendering path to infer `columns` and set wide-field `colSpan`.
- Add integration tests covering inferred columns for Modal/Drawer variants and an explicit columns override case (Modal).
- Update `ROADMAP.md` to mark the Modal/Drawer auto-layout work as complete.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-form/src/ModalForm.tsx | Calls `applyAutoLayout` for flat fields so columns/colSpan are inferred when `schema.columns` is unset. |
| packages/plugin-form/src/DrawerForm.tsx | Same auto-layout application as ModalForm for flat fields. |
| packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/NewVariants.test.tsx | Adds integration tests asserting auto-layout behavior for ModalForm/DrawerForm. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks the form-variant auto-layout task as complete. |

In the doc comment, "apply applyAutoLayout" is duplicated. Consider rephrasing to "call applyAutoLayout" to avoid confusion.
```suggestion
 * These tests verify that ModalForm and DrawerForm call applyAutoLayout
```

These assertions depend on `columns` being forwarded to the rendered <form> as a non-standard DOM attribute (via SchemaRenderer prop spreading). That behavior is an implementation detail and could change; the test would become brittle. Prefer asserting on the layout container classes (e.g. `sm:grid-cols-2` / `md:grid-cols-3`) or another stable indicator of multi-column layout.

DrawerForm’s flat-fields path now runs `applyAutoLayout`, but the integration tests only cover inferred 2 columns and the <=3 field case. Adding a DrawerForm test for an explicit `schema.columns` override (like the ModalForm case) would better validate the new behavior.
